topic: How much more it costs to make chips in the US than in Taiwan
disagreement: SIA/BCG: US 10-year TCO ~25-30% above Taiwan; IC Knowledge: TSMC Arizona wafer cost 7% higher (17% with smaller scale); Morris Chang: 50% higher, later 'could be twice'; Lisa Su: Arizona chips 5-20% more; TSMC: 2-4 points of corporate gross-margin dilution.
possible_reasons: definition: BCG measures TCO after incentives (40-70% of its gap is subsidies); IC Knowledge measures wafer COGS before incentives
population: Chang refers to a 1990s 200mm Oregon fab; IC Knowledge and Su refer to 5nm/4nm Arizona
scale: IC Knowledge attributes 10 of its 17 points to a 20k wpm fab vs 80k wpm Taiwan phases
metric: Su quotes customer price, TSMC quotes consolidated margin impact, not per-wafer cost
time: start-up costs (first fab, new workforce) vs steady state
rationale: The figures measure different things (TCO incl. subsidies, wafer COGS, customer price, consolidated margin) for different fabs and years; once scope is stated most are not in direct conflict, but Chang's 'twice' has no method behind it.
remaining_uncertainty: No method-disclosed estimate of TSMC Arizona's actual steady-state wafer cost vs Taiwan exists in public; TechInsights' 2025 model result is paywalled.

disagreement: TSMC's February 2024 release planned ~86.5% TSMC ownership of JASM after the fab-2 investment; TSMC's 2025 annual report subsidiaries chart shows 73%.
possible_reasons: period: planned post-transaction stake (2024) vs actual at 31 Dec 2025
definition: direct vs effective shareholding or voting vs economic share
later capital injections by minority partners changed the split
rationale: The annual report is a later audited-period disclosure; the press release states a plan subject to closing conditions.
remaining_uncertainty: Why the stake differs (and who holds the remaining 27%) was not found in the opened sources.

topic: What Morris Chang said about the US cost premium
disagreement: Taipei Times (2022) reports Chang saying Oregon chips cost 50% more than Taiwan; TechInsights (2025) paraphrases Chang as saying it would cost TSMC '150% more' to build a new US fab.
possible_reasons: definition: '150%' as an index (Taiwan = 100) equals 50% more; TechInsights' wording conflates the two
population: chip operating cost (Oregon) vs cost to build a new fab
rationale: The contemporaneous report quotes Chang directly with '50 percent more'; the later paraphrase is second-hand.
remaining_uncertainty: The original Brookings interview transcript was not opened.

topic: Japan's subsidy share for JASM vs its stated one-third rule
disagreement: CSIS describes Japan subsidising up to one-third of capital costs for designated chips; DIGITIMES computes JASM's ¥1.208tn subsidy as about 40% of TSMC's >US$20bn investment.
possible_reasons: definition: the one-third ceiling applies to a different programme (designated conventional devices) than the Post-5G fund used for JASM
currency/period: DIGITIMES mixes a JPY subsidy with a USD investment at an unstated exchange rate
population: 'investment' may exclude parts of eligible cost or include non-eligible items
rationale: Not the same programme or the same denominator; METI primary documents were not reachable in this run.
remaining_uncertainty: METI's official eligible-cost base for JASM fabs 1 and 2 and the subsidy share it implies.
